title: Effect intent lifecycle and one-use activation gate
description: Objective: EffectIntent protocol records and the effect.activate linearization point for one Claude node. SPIDR child 1 of 4, split from task-312c1de3c76a4f1dbd8da5c34e629b0e (External effect supervisor) per human-approved 4-child decomposition 2026-08-08. Design authority: pinned rebuild design lines 771-787 (EffectIntent protocol), 336 (attempt lifecycle), 798 (wrapper pre-activation duties). Deliverable: frozen EffectIntent/EffectClaim/EffectResult/EffectTombstone vocabularies with binding fields (aggregate, expected graph epoch/lease, input binding, predecessor cursor value, desired state, effect-specific idempotency key, runtime observation digest); a pure lifecycle reducer admitting exactly PENDING->CLAIMED->ARMED->ACTIVE->SUCCEEDED|FAILED|UNKNOWN and PENDING|CLAIMED|ARMED->CANCEL_REQUESTED->CANCELLED|UNKNOWN; terminal EffectTombstone dominance over pre-activation intents ONLY; the effect.activate revalidation gate (intent state, epoch/lease/binding, desired state, dependency witnesses, runtime closure comparison against the quote-bound ProviderRuntimeObservation digest, lock identity) that atomically pairs effect ARMED->ACTIVE with owning attempt LAUNCH_REQUESTED->RUNNING — together or neither — and returns a one-use activation grant bound to the requesting wrapper; cancel-commits-first rejects activation with no external-action grant, activation-commits-first forces any later cancel into active drain semantics. NOT in scope: OS locks, process observation/adoption, drain/restart reconciliation (child 2), daemon services (child 3), race harness (child 4), Codex, multi-node. Hard dependencies: Claude runtime adapter (task-5ff2b39d, DONE — ProviderRuntimeObservation/observationDigest shapes in packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-observation.ts); Lease presence core (task-967769ea, DONE — lease/epoch shapes MIRRORED STRUCTURALLY: @moe/runner depends only on @moe/contracts and package.json is not owned, follow the claude-render structural-mirror precedent with pinned version literals). Owned paths: packages/runner/src/supervisor/** (greenfield — git ls-files shows no such directory) and its focused tests. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: The lifecycle reducer admits exactly the design-774/775 arcs; every illegal transition is refused with a stable reason code naming the current state and the attempted command, asserted per transition from a generated matrix whose case count is itself asserted nonzero.
A terminal EffectTombstone dominates PENDING|CLAIMED|ARMED and never dominates ACTIVE or later; both directions asserted with their reason codes.

effect.activate returns a ONE-USE grant: a second use of the same grant is refused with a stable code; activation pairs effect ARMED->ACTIVE with attempt LAUNCH_REQUESTED->RUNNING together or neither — a failure injected at each revalidation leg leaves BOTH records unchanged, asserted per leg with the leg-naming code.
Cancel-before-activate rejects activation with a stable code and yields no grant; activate-before-cancel yields active drain semantics; both interleavings tested.

A runtime observation digest mismatch refuses activation with a stable capability-changed code; the focused runner typecheck and test command exits 0 and only explicitly owned paths are staged and committed.
taskRails: Follow pinned design lines 771-787/336/798; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
No child_process, spawn, kill, Date.now, or Math.random anywhere in the module — process facts are caller-supplied observations (adapter fence precedent); timestamps and randomness are inputs.
Mirror scheduler/adapter shapes structurally with pinned version literals; do NOT add dependencies to packages/runner/package.json (not owned).
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Commit by explicit pathspec only.
Assert the reason code and, where more than one layer can refuse, which layer refused; mutation-verify each failure-path test by flipping the production check and confirming red.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 1+2+4 (kernel). Create supervisor/effect-kernel.ts — NO .js bridge (runner convention: zero bridge files; NodeNext resolves .js specifiers to .ts; do NOT touch packages/runner/src/index.ts — claude modules are precedent for unexported internals). CONTENT: (1) frozen vocabularies: EFFECT_STATES = PENDING|CLAIMED|ARMED|ACTIVE|CANCEL_REQUESTED|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|UNKNOWN|CANCELLED with TERMINAL_EFFECT_STATES = SUCCEEDED|FAILED|UNKNOWN|CANCELLED; command vocabulary (claim, arm, activate, requestCancel, settle, consumeGrant); closed error-code list including EFFECT_TOMBSTONED, ATTEMPT_BINDING_MISMATCH, ATTEMPT_NOT_LAUNCH_REQUESTED, and settlement-evidence codes. (2) Records, ALL fields required (never optional — exactOptionalPropertyTypes is on; absent facts are explicit null, adapter precedent): EffectIntent {intentId, aggregateId, expectedGraphEpoch, leaseBinding (mirrored lease record — see step 5), inputBinding, predecessorCursor (opaque string), desiredState, idempotencyKey, runtimeObservationDigest, state, version (safe-integer counter)}; AttemptSlice {attemptId, aggregateId, intentId, state (LAUNCH_REQUESTED|RUNNING slice), version}; EffectTombstone {intentId, reason, terminalizedAt}; ActivationGrant {grantId, intentId, wrapperIdentity, state UNUSED|CONSUMED, version}; provider-NEUTRAL SupervisorFailure shape mirroring claudeFailure's pattern (do not import or reuse ClaudeFailure — supervisor must serve Codex later; do not reuse the six ClaudeReconciledOutcome string values; the interface name MoeEffectIdentity is taken in claude-stream.ts). (3) Full-strictness parsers per scheduler's exactRecord discipline: exact own-key sets (defeats prototype/getter smuggling), safe-integer counters ONLY (canonicalJson THROWS on bigint and on unsafe/float numbers — canonical.ts:16-26; use number, validate like isSafeByteCount), -0 rejected, state vocabulary membership. (4) BYTES RULE: no Uint8Array anywhere in any record — deepFreeze treats one as a plain record and Object.freeze THROWS on a non-empty typed array (canonical.ts:43-62) while canonicalJson would silently digest it as {"0":n} — byte-ish fields are xxxBase64 strings with byteLength/sha256 companions (claude-render precedent). (5) The schema version literal lives on the supervisor ENVELOPE records, never inside the mirrored lease shape (scheduler's LeaseRecord has no version field; injecting one breaks its string-identical-clone convention). (6) MODULE DOC = the CALLER CONTRACT, load-bearing and tested by later steps: (a) effect/attempt/grant successors from one activation commit in ONE transaction with CAS on the intent version AND attempt version read at revalidation; (b) committing an EffectTombstone MUST bump the tombstoned intent's version so a concurrent activation's CAS conflicts — without this the tombstone-vs-activate race is open; (c) grant-id uniqueness and (aggregate, idempotencyKey) uniqueness are store indexes — this pure module validates shape only; (d) the OS-exclusive launch lock (child 2) is the physical duplicate-launch backstop; the grant is only the logical linearization token. Helpers: import canonicalDigest/deepFreeze/sha256Hex from ../canonical.js. Target <=250 lines; split before 400.

No .js bridges (runner convention). No Uint8Array field anywhere; all counters safe-integer number. Version literals on supervisor envelopes only, never inside the mirrored lease shape. pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 3 (lifecycle TDD, RED). Write supervisor/effect-lifecycle.test.ts against the not-yet-written effect-lifecycle.ts. COVER: (1) generated FULL (state x command) matrix — every admitted arc of design 774/775 transitions, every other pair refused with the stable code naming BOTH the current state and attempted command; the generator asserts its own case count equals |states| x |commands| so a silently-empty sweep fails. (2) Kernel parse refusals (hostile fixtures: extra key, getter property, -0 version, unsafe-integer counter, bigint-shaped string where number expected, unknown state) each with exact code. (3) SETTLEMENT IS EVIDENCE-BOUND (verified-attack fix — the reducer must not invent completions): settle(SUCCEEDED|FAILED) REQUIRES a settlement-evidence reference record {reconciliationVersion, reconciliationDigest (hex64), outcomeClass} validated for shape and digest-bound into the terminal record; settle(UNKNOWN) additionally requires an uncertainty-evidence record; missing or malformed evidence is a DISTINCT stable code and zero state change; the terminal record carries the evidence digest verbatim (child 2 binds real reconcileClaudeRun output to this seam — shape only here, no interpretation). (4) Tombstone dominance BOTH directions: applies to PENDING|CLAIMED|ARMED; refused with its own code against ACTIVE|CANCEL_REQUESTED|terminals. (5) Terminal absorption cross-product: every command against each of SUCCEEDED|FAILED|UNKNOWN|CANCELLED refused naming both. (6) requestCancel on ACTIVE returns the THIRD outcome kind MUST_DRAIN — typed as neither ok:true nor ok:false refusal; it asserts both records are active and drain is mandatory (drain itself is child 2); a naive refusal-shaped MUST_DRAIN is wrong because callers pattern-matching refusal codes would retry an instruction. (7) The admitted-transition TABLE is exported DATA (frozen array), and the exhaustive test derives from it — the declared child-2 extension seam: child 2 adds the design-776 ACTIVE->CANCEL_REQUESTED edge by extending the table, not rewriting this test. (8) CANCELLED vs UNKNOWN cancel arcs discriminated by input evidence kind. Suite RED for module-missing, not import-crash.

Also added effect-test-fixtures.ts (scheduler authority/test-fixtures.ts precedent) with unknown-typed overrides so hostile shapes are expressible.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 4 (lifecycle GREEN). supervisor/effect-lifecycle.ts: pure reducer over kernel records — records in, ONE frozen result out (deepFreeze; remember the no-typed-array rule); zero clocks/randomness (timestamps are validated inputs); admitted transitions driven by the exported frozen TABLE from the kernel/lifecycle boundary; every refusal is a SupervisorFailure carrying code + the (state, command) pair; MUST_DRAIN third outcome kind; settlement evidence digest-bound via canonicalDigest; version increments by exactly 1 on every state change and 0 on refusal (lease-core rule: versionDelta in {0,1}, state change implies 1). Gate: step-2 suite green via pnpm --filter @moe/runner test. Target <=250 lines.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN: 86/86 tests pass, typecheck exit 0. effect-lifecycle.ts (253 lines) is a pure reducer — no clock, no randomness, timestamps are validated inputs. ADMITTED_EFFECT_TRANSITIONS is an exported deep-frozen 8-row table (the child-2 seam for the design-776 ACTIVE->CANCEL_REQUESTED edge); no code path invents an edge that is not in it. LifecycleOutcome has three kinds discriminated by `kind`: TRANSITIONED (ok:true, versionDelta 1), MUST_DRAIN (drainRequired:true, versionDelta 0, NO `ok` field at all so a caller matching ok:false cannot mistake it for a rejected command), REFUSED (exactly {kind,failure}, no successor fields). The RED run caught a real imprecision: routing settle straight to the evidence gate made "PENDING does not admit settle at all" report EFFECT_SETTLEMENT_TARGET_NOT_ADMITTED; production now splits arc-missing (EFFECT_TRANSITION_NOT_ADMITTED) from target-not-in-arc, so the two mistakes stay distinguishable to a caller. Settlement digest = canonicalDigest({settlement, uncertainty}) bound into EffectResult; tombstone dominance restricted to PENDING|CLAIMED|ARMED and to a tombstone naming the same intent.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 3 (activation TDD, RED). Write supervisor/effect-activation.test.ts. LEG ORDER (integrity/identity before authority before content, digest LAST; first failing leg decides the code, exactly once): 1 intent is ARMED + claim/lock identity matches; 2 TOMBSTONE WITNESS — activate TAKES tombstone: EffectTombstone | null as an INPUT and refuses EFFECT_TOMBSTONED when non-null (BLOCKER fix: a pure function cannot refuse on a record it is never given; the caller-contract version-bump clause from step 1 is what closes the commit-side race — assert the doc states it); 3 ATTEMPT_BINDING_MISMATCH (attempt id/aggregate/intent binding); 4 ATTEMPT_NOT_LAUNCH_REQUESTED; 5 graph epoch equality; 6 lease fence via the strict mirror (step 5); 7 desired-state match; 8 dependency witnesses current; 9 runtimeObservationDigest equality (compare digest STRINGS — the wrapper convention per claude-observation.ts:190-217). TESTS: per-leg injected failure → exact code AND structurally zero state change (refusal object contains NO successor fields; frozen inputs unmutated); double-fault input → earlier leg's code exactly once; cancel-commits-first (CANCEL_REQUESTED, CANCELLED, and tombstoned variants) refuses with no grant; activate-before-cancel → later requestCancel is MUST_DRAIN. SUCCESS: one frozen ActivationCommit envelope carrying effect ARMED->ACTIVE successor + attempt LAUNCH_REQUESTED->RUNNING successor + UNUSED ActivationGrant + activationDigest = canonicalDigest over all three successors; grantId is DETERMINISTIC from (intentId, activationDigest) so a replayed activation cannot mint a fresh grant id. GRANT: consumeActivationGrant(grant, wrapperIdentity) returns CONSUMED successor; consuming a CONSUMED grant refused with stable code; different wrapperIdentity refused with its own code; HONESTY TEST (verified-attack requirement): re-presenting the SAME stale UNUSED record succeeds at the pure layer — asserted AS success — pinning that replay protection is the caller's CAS + store uniqueness + OS launch lock, not this function. PARTIAL-COMMIT DETECTOR: validateActivationCommit(effect, attempt, grant) refuses/flags effect ACTIVE with attempt not RUNNING (and grant/digest mismatches) so a rehydrating caller can machine-check the together-or-neither invariant after restart.
implementationPlan.note: RED verified: activation suite fails on `Failed to resolve import "./effect-activation.js"` while the lifecycle suite stays green (86 passed). effect-activation.test.ts pins a 10-entry LEG table (count asserted) in the design order intentState, lockIdentity, tombstoneWitness, attemptBinding, attemptState, graphEpoch, leaseFence, desiredState, dependencyWitness, runtimeObservation — each injected failure asserts code AND layer AND detail.leg, plus structurally zero state change (refusal key set is exactly {kind,failure}; the whole request's canonicalDigest is compared before/after). Double-fault (attemptBinding + graphEpoch) asserts the earlier code and that the later code appears nowhere in the serialized outcome. Tombstone is an activate INPUT so a pure function can actually witness it; a separate test asserts EFFECT_CALLER_CONTRACT publishes the "EffectTombstone MUST bump ... compare-and-set" clause that closes the commit-side race. Cancel-first (CANCEL_REQUESTED and CANCELLED) refuses with no commit field; activate-first then requestCancel yields MUST_DRAIN. Grant id is asserted against a hand-built canonicalDigest({activationDigest, intentId}) so a randomised grantId reddens. Grant honesty test asserts SUCCESS on a replayed stale UNUSED record. validateActivationCommit covers ACTIVE-without-RUNNING, undeived grant id, wrong intent, malformed attempt. Redaction tests assert neither lease token nor the expected runtime digest is echoed. Added EFFECT_CLAIM_MALFORMED to the closed code list (30 codes).

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 4 (activation + mirror GREEN). Two production files. supervisor/lease-mirror.ts: STRICT structural re-validation of the mirrored lease record — NOT a trusting shape cast (verified-attack finding: a token/epoch comparison on unparsed shapes accepts records scheduler's parseLeaseRecord refuses — a fencing bypass). Clone the parse discipline at full strictness: exact own-key set, isCount semantics (rejects -0, non-safe integers, values above the authority-count ceiling — mirror the two-bound rule: parse <= ceiling, mutate < ceiling), state vocabulary, then fence checks in lease-fencing's published order (token, epoch, hash, session, version, state) with malformed-parse-first yielding a PLAIN refusal carrying no security detail. REDACTION RULE (both files): no refusal may carry the input leaseToken or the expected observation digest value — scheduler redacts these deliberately; supervisor must not leak them. supervisor/effect-activation.ts: the 9-leg gate + ActivationCommit envelope + deterministic grant + consumeActivationGrant + validateActivationCommit per step 4's tests. Cross-package NOTE for planningNotes/handoff: runner tests CANNOT import @moe/scheduler (single-dep package; cross-package relative imports break composite rootDir) — the mirror's hostile fixtures here assert supervisor verdicts only; the verdict-EQUALITY drift test against scheduler's real fenceAuthority lands in child 4 via the daemon package, which will have BOTH deps after child 3's ownership amendment. Gate: steps 2+4 suites green. Target <=250 lines each; if effect-activation.ts bursts toward 400, split the grant/validator pair into a fifth prod file (per-file cap is the rail; file COUNT is not).

Three production files (the plan's declared split of the grant/validator pair into a fifth file was taken; per-file cap is the rail, file count is not): lease-mirror.ts (112) re-VALIDATES the mirrored lease and proof through parseMirroredLease/parseMirroredProof before any comparison — not a shape cast — then fences in the scheduler's published order (token, epoch with the REVOKED/superseded discrimination, authority hash, session, version, state) with malformed-parse-first and exhausted-counter both answered plainly and with state:null so a syntactically invalid attempt carries no security detail; 4 mirror codes map 1:1 onto scheduler's 4 authority codes so child 4's verdict-equality drift test in the daemon package is a clean mapping. effect-grant.ts (148) derives grantId = canonicalDigest({activationDigest, intentId}) from the identity-free initialGrantBinding (state UNUSED, version 0), so consumption does not change the derivation and validateActivationCommit can still machine-check a rehydrated triple; consumeActivationGrant checks wrapper identity before grant state. effect-activation.ts (233) parses the request envelope with an exact 11-key set, then runs the legs in order counters, intentState, lockIdentity, tombstoneWitness, attemptBinding, attemptState, graphEpoch, leaseFence (mirror failure restamped via withLeg so both the deciding layer AND the leg are on the record), desiredState, dependencyWitness, runtimeObservation — digest STRING comparison only, concrete digests never enter a refusal. Also removed an unreachable claim-null branch surfaced while tightening ParsedRequest.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 3+4 (property, redaction, hostile-mirror tests). Write supervisor/effect-properties.test.ts: (1) digest replay property — structurally equal EffectIntent/ActivationCommit values produce IDENTICAL canonicalDigest; key insertion order does not change it (canonicalJson sorts keys — assert it via two construction orders); (2) redaction sweep — every refusal constructor in the module is enumerated (generated list, count asserted equal to the closed error-code list length) and JSON.stringify of each refusal contains neither the input leaseToken value nor the expected observation digest value; (3) hostile-mirror fixture matrix — extra key, accessor property, -0 epoch, counter above ceiling, wrong state vocabulary, exhausted counter — each refused with the mirror's exact code and the malformed-first ordering asserted (a record failing both parse and fence yields the parse code); (4) counter-ceiling two-bound rule asserted on every mirrored/versioned field (parse accepts == ceiling, transition refuses to exceed); (5) frozen-result property — every success and refusal output is deep-frozen and every input remains unmutated (compare pre/post canonicalDigest of inputs).
implementationPlan.note: GREEN: 230/230 tests across 3 supervisor suites, typecheck exit 0. effect-properties.test.ts (226) adds: (1) a refusal sweep that drives ALL 30 closed codes from real production surfaces — asserts observed.length === SUPERVISOR_ERROR_CODES.length AND set equality, so an unreachable code (a code no surface can produce) fails the suite rather than hiding; each of the 30 then gets a code assertion, a redaction assertion (neither lease token value nor the expected runtime observation digest appears in JSON.stringify), and a deep-frozen assertion on outcome/failure/detail. (2) Hostile mirror matrix: extra key, accessor, -0 epoch, above-ceiling counter, unknown state, unknown kind — all LEASE_MIRROR_MALFORMED; malformed-first ordering asserted by a record that fails BOTH parse and fence (yields the parse code with detail.state null); malformed detail asserted to be exactly {state:null, command:"effect.activate", leg:null}, i.e. no security detail. (3) Counter-ceiling two-bound rule: parseEffectIntent/parseMirroredLease ACCEPT a record at the ceiling (asserted non-null) while applyEffectCommand and activateEffect refuse EFFECT_COUNTER_EXHAUSTED, and one past the ceiling is refused at parse time. (4) Digest replay: a key-order-reversed intent digests identically, with a guard assertion that the key orders really do differ so the test cannot pass vacuously. (5) Frozen-success property plus inputs unchanged by pre/post canonicalDigest of the whole request. Also changed lease-mirror's FENCED success from Object.freeze to deepFreeze so the frozen-output property holds for the nested lease/proof too.

implementationPlan.note:
MUTATION DRILL — 9 mutations, each applied at the mechanism's single source, backed up out-of-tree, restore verified by git hash-object diff, green re-confirmed after every one. (1) tombstone-witness leg disabled -> 6 red incl. the tombstoned-activate test; (2) attemptBinding/graphEpoch legs swapped -> exactly the double-fault leg-order test red; (3) ARMED/activate row deleted from the table -> BOTH the hand-written-arcs equality test and the 'ARMED x activate' matrix cell red, proving the expectations are not derived from the table under test; (4) settle evidence requirement dropped -> evidence-refusal test red AND the sweep's completeness assertion red; (5) grantId minted from a counter instead of derived -> derivation, replay, and coherent-triple tests red; (6) mirror isCount accepts -0 -> both -0 fixtures red; (7) mirror refusal interpolates the lease token -> both redaction sweeps red; (8) version bump skipped -> all 8 admitted-arc matrix cells red; (9) witness list back to Array.isArray + for..of -> the two new hostile-array tests red.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — one real defect found and FIXED: parseWitnessList used Array.isArray + for...of, which accepts a subclassed array whose Symbol.iterator answers different elements than the length check saw, and reads accessor elements. Replaced with a readList clone of the scheduler's discipline (plain-array prototype check, own-data length and element reads, 128 cap); four hostile fixtures added and mutation-verified. NOTED, not defects: an empty witness list legitimately asserts "no dependencies" and this function cannot distinguish that from a caller that failed to load them — documented as a store responsibility; EFFECT_COUNTER_EXHAUSTED is reachable from two layers (LIFECYCLE and ACTIVATION) which the layer field discriminates; the tombstone that commits AFTER revalidation is out of reach of any pure function and is closed by the published caller-contract version-bump clause. No shared state, no handles/sockets/subprocesses, so no error-path cleanup exists to leak.

CHECKLIST: grep for child_process/spawn/kill/Date.now/Math.random/new Date/performance.now across all supervisor files = 0 hits; no Uint8Array/ArrayBuffer/Buffer field (only the kernel doc line explaining why); wc -l (not Measure-Object) max production file 257, all <=304 incl. tests; no probe/scratch files; long lines wrapped to <=115 except the 4 EFFECT_CALLER_CONTRACT string literals whose exact text a test asserts. 235/235 green, typecheck exit 0.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Settlement arcs: (a) evidence-bound settle commands now vs (b) defer all ACTIVE->terminal arcs to child 2 with a SETTLEMENT_DEFERRED refusal. Chose (a)-lite — settle requires a shape-validated evidence reference (reconciliationVersion/digest/outcomeClass) digest-bound into the terminal record, no interpretation — because the task DoD pins 'admits exactly the design-774/775 arcs' and (b) would contradict it; child 2 binds real reconcileClaudeRun output to the same seam. Tombstone handling: adversarial review proved the original design UNSATISFIABLE (BLOCKER) — a pure activate cannot refuse on a tombstone it is never given, and CAS on the intent alone does not conflict with a separate tombstone row; fixed by making tombstone an explicit activation INPUT plus the caller-contract clause that tombstone commit bumps the intent version. Grant replay: chose honesty over overclaim — the pure layer PROVABLY cannot refuse a stale UNUSED replay; the plan pins that as an asserted-success test and names the caller CAS + store uniqueness + OS launch lock (child 2) as the real guards. Failure shape: provider-neutral SupervisorFailure, NOT ClaudeFailure reuse — supervisor must serve Codex later.
